text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All dailies lead with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's statement that relations with Singapore will normalise as soon as Malasyians get over their feeling of hurt and bitterness caused by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's derogatory remarks about a Malaysia state.
-- Academicians, businessmen and leaders of youth movements say they support the move for a "cooling off" in relations with Singapore.
-- Mahathir says Japan should admit that its troops had committed atrocities during World War II instead of trying to revise its history books.
-- Work on the second link bridge connecting Malaysia and Singapore will go on, Works Minister S. Samy Vellu says.
